title: Universal Governance entrypoint — ATLAS_RECORD first
issue_presented: How must an Atlas agent resolve current universal law when historical Governance artifacts remain visible?

known_facts.fact: User Order 2026-08-23 requires every agent to begin governance resolution from ATLAS_RECORD/CURRENT_LAW.md.
Finding F-V2-1 was that the public Atlas-Governance README could still appear authoritative if opened directly.

analysis: Availability of an older repo is not authority. The public historical README may carry a supersession banner. V2 startup guidance must state the six-step resolution order. Failure to resolve the pointer is UNKNOWN or USER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, not silent fallback.
judgment_rule: Every Atlas agent must begin governance resolution from ATLAS_RECORD/CURRENT_LAW.md (or the equivalent designated pointer in its environment).

The agent must not determine current universal Atlas law merely by encountering an older Governance repository, JUDGMENT.md, local docket, overlay, Clerk/Magistrate workflow, or historical artifact first.
If the current-law pointer cannot be resolved, classify authority as UNKNOWN or USER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED. Do not silently fall back to a historical source.
Historical sources may be used for governing_law_at_time and watcher-only operation after current law is resolved.
Onboarding text lives in STARTUP.md. Public historical README may name Atlas-Governance-V2 and ATLAS_RECORD but must not publish private V2 contents, private judgments, or private source.
operational_effect: STARTUP.md is mandatory onboarding. Public historical README carries a HISTORICAL banner. F-V2-1 closes when validation of those two surfaces PASSES.
exceptions: WATCHER_ONLY overlay in the historical repo may still run; that does not restore universal-law authority.
required_validation: Banner at top of public README; STARTUP.md six-step order; no private V2 SHA/source in public README; overlay hashes unchanged; historical job-law attribution unchanged.
